questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Astute
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Astute
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Stupid.

Key Points

  • The word "Astute" means having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage. (चतुर)
    • Example: He was an astute businessman who could easily identify the best investment opportunities.
  • "Stupid" refers to lacking intelligence or common sense. (मूर्ख)
    • Example: It was stupid of him to forget the keys inside the car.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Astute' is 'Stupid'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Stupid.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Temporary (अस्थायी): Lasting for only a limited period of time.
    • Example: The temporary suspension of the service caused inconvenience to the users.
  • Illegal (अवैध): Contrary to or forbidden by law.
    • Example: Illegal activities such as smuggling are severely punishable.
  • Dispute (विवाद): A disagreement or argument.
    • Example: The land dispute between the neighbors has been going on for years.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a. This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually. b. The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually. c. While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so. d. It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

a. This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually.
b. The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually.
c. While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so.
d. It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The paragraph provides a comparative analysis of the urban and rural population trends in India and the US.
  • Sentence B is the first sentence as it presents the data on India's urban and rural population growth rates:
    • "The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually."
  • Sentence D follows as it relates to the comparison mentioned in sentence B:
    • "It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas."
  • Sentence C is the third sentence because it provides the current percentages of urban populations in the US and India:
    • "While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so."
  • Sentence A is the fourth as it discusses the prediction related to the US population:
    • "This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually."
  • The correct sequence is BDCA.
 
Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:
"The United Nations reports that India’s urban population is growing at a rate of 1.1 percent annually, while the country's rural population is shrinking at a rate of 0.37 percent annually. It's still a considerably smaller percentage of the Indian population than it is in the US that resides in urban areas. While 82% of Americans live in urban settings, only 30% of Indians do so. This figure is predicted to climb as the percentage of Americans residing in rural areas falls by an average of 1.6% annually."

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) to become severely seasick (B) a world tour, but he was (C) a nervous flyer and tended (D) he wanted to go on
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) to become severely seasick
(B) a world tour, but he was
(C) a nervous flyer and tended
(D) he wanted to go on
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence describes someone's conflicting desires and conditions: wanting to go on a world tour while dealing with fears and health issues related to travel.
  • Part D is the first part as it initiates the subject's desire: "he wanted to go on".
  • Part B follows providing the object of the desire: "a world tour, but he was".
  • Part C is next detailing his condition: "a nervous flyer and tended".
  • Part A completes the sentence by adding the second condition: "to become severely seasick".
  • The correct sequence is DBCA.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"He wanted to go on a world tour, but he was a nervous flyer and tended to become severely seasick."

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. A famous company conducted the workshop for its customers.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
A famous company conducted the workshop for its customers.

options.text: The workshop were conducted by a famous company for its customers.
options.html: The workshop were conducted by a famous company for its customers.

options.text: The workshop had been conducted by a famous company for its customers.
options.html: The workshop had been conducted by a famous company for its customers.

options.text: The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers.
options.html: The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers.

options.text: The workshop is conducted by a famous company for its customers.
options.html: The workshop is conducted by a famous company for its customers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "A famous company conducted the workshop for its customers."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the workshop" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "conducted" to "was conducted" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "a famous company."
  • Ensure the prepositional phrase "for its customers" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The workshop was conducted by a famous company for its customers."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "The workshop were conducted by a famous company for its customers." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement.
  • Option 2: "The workshop had been conducted by a famous company for its customers." – Incorrect past perfect tense.
  • Option 4: "The workshop is conducted by a famous company for its customers." – Incorrect present simple tense.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. She ________ requested him to pay the bills. (persistently)

    • Example: She persistently called every day to check on the status of her application.
  • "Continuously" refers to something that happens without stopping or being interrupted. (लगातार)
    • Example: The river flowed continuously through the valley.
  • Hence, we can infer that a synonym for 'persistently' is 'continuously'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate set of ANTONYMS of the highlighted word. 'Grisly' The other day Jimmy behaved ______ with Jammy and that was quite ______ for me.
questions.questionHtml:
Complete the sentence with the most appropriate set of ANTONYMS of the highlighted word.
'Grisly'
The other day Jimmy behaved ______ with Jammy and that was quite ______ for me.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The word "Grisly" means something that is causing horror or disgust. (भयानक)
    • Example: The grisly scene of the accident left everyone in shock.
  • "Pleasantly" refers to something that is enjoyable, pleasing, or agreeable. (सुखद)
    • Example: She was pleasantly surprised by the unexpected gift.
  • "Comforting" means providing comfort or solace. (सांत्वना देने वाला)
    • Example: His comforting words helped ease her anxiety.
  • Hence, we can infer that the antonyms of 'Grisly' are 'Pleasantly' and 'Comforting'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: Rudely, attractive
    • Rudely (असभ्यतापूर्वक): In an impolite or disrespectful manner.
      • Example: He rudely interrupted the speaker in the middle of the presentation.
    • Attractive (आकर्षक): Pleasing or appealing to the senses.
      • Example: The garden was filled with attractive flowers and plants.
  • Option 2: Disgusting, atrocious
    • Disgusting (घिनौना): Arousing revulsion or strong indignation.
      • Example: The food was disgusting and had a foul odor.
    • Atrocious (क्रूर): Horrifyingly wicked or of a very poor quality.
      • Example: The atrocious crime shocked the entire community.
  • Option 3: Ghastly, shameless
    • Ghastly (भयानक): Causing great horror or fear.
      • Example: The ghastly sight of the haunted house scared the children.
    • Shameless (बेशर्म): Showing a lack of shame or modesty.
      • Example: His shameless behavior at the party was unacceptable.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) one of the primary obstacles encountered (b) is the risk of sample contamination (c) during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS) (d) from improper handling and collecting methodologies (e) proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(a) one of the primary obstacles encountered
(b) is the risk of sample contamination
(c) during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS)
(d) from improper handling and collecting methodologies
(e) proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. acebd.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence identifies a specific technical challenge within the field of forensic investigation and substance analysis.
  • Part (a) is the first part as it introduces the primary subject: "one of the primary obstacles encountered".
  • Part (c) follows to provide the context of the struggle: "during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS)". This connects the "obstacles" to a specific scientific process.
  • Part (e) is the third part as it lists the specific forensic evidence being analyzed alongside CDS: "proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence".
  • Part (b) follows as it introduces the linking verb 'is' and defines the obstacle: "is the risk of sample contamination".
  • Part (d) is the final part as it explains the origin or cause of the aforementioned risk: "from improper handling and collecting methodologies".
  • The correct sequence is acebd.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"One of the primary obstacles encountered during the analysis of controlled dangerous substance (CDS) proof bloodstain patterns and DNA evidence is the risk of sample contamination from improper handling and collecting methodologies."
 
Additional Information
  • Structural Breakdown: The sentence follows a standard Subject + Qualifier + Verb + Complement pattern.
    • Subject: One of the primary obstacles (a)
    • Qualifier: encountered during the analysis... (c + e)
    • Verb: is (b)
    • Complement: the risk of sample contamination... (b + d)
  • Forensic Context: In forensic science, "Controlled Dangerous Substances" (CDS) and "DNA evidence" are highly sensitive to "contamination," making the link between parts (b) and (d) logically essential.
